JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sunil Kumar S. caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 2-3-2023 at about 13.30 p.m. when Sunil Kumar was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ET-3821 on Hosakote-Chinthamani SH 82 road on the extreme left side of the road, near Pakashala hotel,
Doddahulluru- Sonnadenahalli gate middle, at that time, driver of the car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314 came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed behind the Sunil Kumar vehicle,
due to sudden impact Sunil Kumar sustained grievous fatal injuries and he was shifted to nearby hospital, but due to savior head head injury, he died on the way to hospital.

It is further stated that immediately Sunil Kumar was shifted to Hosakote Government hospital for post mortem and after postmortem was conducted the dead-body was handed over to the legal representative of the Sunil Kumar.
It is further stated that petitioners were spent Rs.1 lakh towards conveyance, transportation and funeral expenses.

It is further stated that Sunil Kumar was aged about 30 years and was working as a driver at different owners and earning more than Rs.30,000/-p.m. and contributing his entire income to the welfare of the family.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.40 lakhs from the respondents.
3. After service of notice to respondents, the respondent No.1 remained exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel before this Tribunal and filed written statement wherein contended that there is a violation of section 134(c) of MV Act and 158(c) of MV Act.
The driver of the car was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Sunil Kumar S died due to the grievous injury sustained by him in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314 on 02-03-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. near Pakashala hotel, Doddahulluru- Sonnadenahalli gate middle, Chinthamani road, SH- 82, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru rural and he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :

ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex-P1 to 12 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch,
seizure mahazar, inquest report, PM report, col.133 notice, reply to notice, charge sheet, adhar card,
DL.
9.
On perusal of the records discloses that soon after the accident, petitioner lodged the complaint as per Ex-P2 before the Hoskote Traffic police.

Thereafter Hoskote traffic police registered FIR as per Ex-P1 and conducted thorough and detailed investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex- P10 against the Abilash B.N. driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314 for the offence punishable under Secs. 279, 304-A of IPC by holding that on 2-3-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. accused driver of the car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314 by name Abilash drove the car in speed, rash and negligent manner from Hoskote towards Chinthamani on the National High Way-82 and near Pakashala hotel in front of Essar Petrol Bunk, near Doddahulluru Village hit to the deceased Sunil Kumar, who was riding Apachi bike bearing No.KA-01- ET-3821 in the same direction while trying to over take the said bike, hit to the back side of the said bike and due to the speed of the Fortuner car, the bike has fallen about 20 to 30 feet away from the spot and rider of the bike Sunil Kumar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on the way to the hospital.
The respondent has not placed any materials and evidence to show that the charge sheet Ex.P.10 filed by the concerned police is defective and collusive.
10. Apart from this on perusal of Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Sketch at Ex.P.4 it clearly shows that the accident has been taken place in the middle of the High way road.
Thus, Ex.P.4 clearly demonstrate that the driver of the offending car while overtaking the bike moving in front of him has hit to the back portion of the bike and thereby caused accident.
Ex. P.7-
Motor Vehicle report clearly shows the damages caused to both the vehicles due to the accident and report shows that the accident has taken place not due to the mechanical defect of the vehicle.

Respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having the DL and the vehicle was not having the FC, but the jurisdictional police after detailed and through investigation has filed the charge sheet which does not discloses that driver of the offending vehicle was not having the DL.
Hence the contention of the respondent is not acceptable.

sentences.text: At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
12. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
13. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle car bearing No.KA-67-M-1314.
14.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

15. ISSUES NO.2 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother of Sunil Kumar S.
The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P11-Copy of Aadhaar card and Ex-P12-copy of DL of the deceased Sunil Kumar S.
From the said Ex-P11 and 12, it reveals that petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and mother of the deceased Sunil Kumar S.
Hence issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

16. ISSUES NO.3: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS: From Ex-P12 Copy of DL of Sunil Kumar S., it reveals that Sunil Kumar S. date of birth is 6-4-1992 and as on the date of accident, Sunil Kumar S. was aged 30 years.
Admittedly the deceased was bachelor and the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 26-30 is '17'.
17. PW-1 has stated in his affidavit that deceased Sunil Kumar was working as driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents regarding the avocation and income of Sunil Kumar S..

Hence notional income of the deceased Sunil Kumar S. is taken as Rs.16,000/-p.m.
18.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 30 years.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157,
40% of income is to be added towards future prospects in case of self employed.

40% of Rs.16,000/-

Therefore the total income comes to Rs.22,400/- (16,000+6,400).

Admittedly, the deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.22,400/- works out to Rs.11,200/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.11,200/- (22,400-11,200).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,34,400/- (11,200 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '17'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.22,84,800/- (1,34,400 X 17).
19. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of filial consortium and loss of love & affection.

21. FUNERAL EXPENSES:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,

Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.24,17,900/-.
23. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

24. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 is insurer is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'
and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;

The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
